intro: Ser means to be for identity, origin, profession, character, time and dates: things seen as essential or lasting. It's completely irregular and one of the most used verbs in the language.

presente.en: The house is big and pretty.
We've been friends for many years.

perfeito.en: I was the first to arrive.

imperfeito.en: When I was a child, I lived in Porto.
You were very shy as a child.

imperfeito.pt: A casa dos meus avós [era] muito antiga.
imperfeito.en: My grandparents' house was very old.
We used to be neighbours.

futuro.en: This year I will be your teacher.
You will always be welcome here.
Tomorrow will be an important day.
The results will be published on Friday.

condicional.en: It would be great to go to the beach.
I would be happier in the countryside.
Would you be able to help me?
We would be good neighbours.

perfeito.en: They were very kind to me.

imperfeito.en: When I was young, I was very shy.
imperfeito.pt: Quando era novo, era muito tímido.

imperfeito.en: The house was very old.
It was ten o'clock.

futuro.en: It's going to be difficult.
The party will be on Saturday.
futuro.pt: A festa vai ser no sábado.

futuro.en: You're going to be a good doctor.

condicional.en: It would be better to wait.
Would it be possible to change table?
That would be fantastic.

notes.presente: Ser is for what something is: identity, nationality, profession, character, time, dates, and where an event takes place (A festa é em casa da Ana). For moods, temporary states and where people or things are, use estar.
notes.perfeito: Ser and ir share the same perfeito: fui, foste, foi, fomos, foram. Context tells you which: Fui professor (I was a teacher) vs Fui a Lisboa (I went to Lisbon).
notes.imperfeito: Use era for descriptions, age and time in the past: Era uma vez... (Once upon a time...), Eram dez horas (It was ten o'clock).
notes.futuro: In speech you'll usually hear ir + infinitivo: vai ser (it's going to be) rather than será.

patterns.en: to be a ... (Sou engenheiro, no article)
what is it that...? (very common question frame)

compare.ex: Ele é simpático, mas hoje está cansado.

recap: Sou de Copenhaga, mas agora estou em Lisboa. (I'm from Copenhagen, but now I'm in Lisbon.)

intro: Ter means to have: possessions, family, age and many feelings (ter fome, ter frio). It's irregular. Ter de + infinitive is the everyday way to say 'to have to'.

presente.en: Do you have a new mobile phone?
We have a meeting at ten.
They have a house in the Algarve.

perfeito.en: I had a very long day.

imperfeito.en: When I was a child, I had a dog.
You used to have long hair.
We didn't have a television at home.
The city had a lot of old cafés.

futuro.en: I will have more time in the summer.
You will have the results tomorrow.
The new hotel will have a pool.
We will have a meeting on Monday.

condicional.pt: Se fosse rico, [teria] uma casa na praia.
condicional.en: If I were rich, I would have a house on the beach.
Would you have time to help me?

condicional.pt: O meu avô [teria] cem anos hoje.
condicional.en: My grandfather would be a hundred today.
Without help, they wouldn't have managed.

perfeito.en: I had a problem with the car.
perfeito.pt: Tive um problema com o carro.

perfeito.en: Did you have a good weekend?
perfeito.pt: Tiveste um bom fim de semana?

imperfeito.en: When I was a child, I had a cat.
imperfeito.pt: Quando era criança, tinha um gato.

imperfeito.en: We didn't have much money.
He was hungry.

futuro.en: I'm going to have a lot of work.
You'll have time tomorrow.
We're going to have to wait.

condicional.en: I would have more time.
Would you have a pen? (formal)
That would make no sense.

notes.presente: Many feelings use ter + noun: ter fome (hungry), ter sede (thirsty), ter frio / calor (cold / hot), ter medo (afraid), ter sono (sleepy). Age too: Tenho 30 anos. Note tem (he/she has) vs têm (they have).
notes.perfeito: Ter de + infinitive = to have to: Tive de esperar (I had to wait). In Portugal ter de is preferred; ter que is also heard.
notes.imperfeito: Use tinha for age and states in the past: Quando tinha dez anos... (When I was ten...).
notes.futuro: Everyday speech uses ir + ter: vou ter, vais ter. Vou ter de trabalhar = I'm going to have to work.

patterns.en: to be hungry / thirsty / cold / hot

compare.ex: Há um café na esquina, mas eu tenho café em casa.

recap: Tenho fome e tenho de comer! (I'm hungry and I have to eat!)

intro: Estar means to be for temporary states, feelings, location and the weather. It's irregular, and it also forms the European Portuguese continuous: estar a + infinitivo (estou a trabalhar).

perfeito.en: I was in Paris last year.

perfeito.pt: O tempo [esteve] ótimo no fim de semana.
perfeito.en: The weather was great at the weekend.
We waited for you for an hour.

imperfeito.en: Yesterday I was very tired.
It was raining when I went out.
We were at home when you called.
They were watching television.

futuro.en: I will be at home at eight.
Tomorrow you'll be better.
Dinner will be ready at nine.

futuro.pt: Eles [estarão] no escritório até às seis.
futuro.en: They will be in the office until six.

condicional.en: Without you, I wouldn't be here.
Would you be available tomorrow?
He would be happy with this news.
We would be better off at the beach.

perfeito.en: I was in Porto last week.
perfeito.pt: Estive no Porto na semana passada.

imperfeito.en: I was tired.
It was raining.
Where were you when I called you?

futuro.en: I'm going to be at work.
Are you going to be at home tonight?
futuro.pt: Vais estar em casa logo à noite?

futuro.en: They're going to be here at five.
futuro.pt: Eles vão estar aqui às cinco.

condicional.en: I would be happier in Portugal.
Would you be available on Friday?
It would be ready tomorrow.

notes.presente: Ser vs estar: ser for what something is (O Pedro é alegre, personality), estar for how or where it is now (O Pedro está triste hoje, mood today; O Pedro está em casa). Estar a + infinitivo is the EP continuous: Estou a ler. Brazil says estou lendo.
notes.perfeito: Estive em = I was in / I've been to: Já estive em Lisboa (I've been to Lisbon).
notes.imperfeito: Estava a + infinitivo describes what was going on: Estava a dormir quando ligaste (I was sleeping when you called).
notes.futuro: In speech prefer ir + infinitivo: vou estar, vais estar. Estarei sounds more formal.

patterns.en: to be hungry / cold / in a hurry (right now)

compare.ex: A sopa é boa, mas hoje está fria.

compare.en: to stay / to end up (a change of state)
compare.ex: Fiquei contente com a notícia.

recap: Estou a aprender português e estou muito contente! (I'm learning Portuguese and I'm very happy!)

intro: In everyday use haver means there is / there are and appears only in the 3rd person singular: há, houve, havia. Há + a time expression also means 'ago' or 'for' (há dois anos).

presente.en: There are a lot of people on the beach.
I've lived in Lisbon for five years.

perfeito.en: There was an accident on the motorway.
Yesterday there was a street party.
There were lots of problems with the flight.
There were no classes on Friday.

imperfeito.en: There were a lot of people at the concert.
There used to be a cinema here.
There was no room in the restaurant.

imperfeito.pt: [Havia] sempre fruta em casa da minha avó.
imperfeito.en: There was always fruit at my grandmother's house.

futuro.en: There will be a concert on Saturday.
Tomorrow there will be sun in the Algarve.
There will be time for everything.
There will be no trains on the public holiday.

condicional.en: Would there be room for one more person?
Without rain, there would be no water.

condicional.pt: Disseram que [haveria] autocarros até à meia-noite.
condicional.en: They said there would be buses until midnight.
Would there be another solution?

presente.en: There's a pharmacy on the corner.
I saw her two days ago.

perfeito.en: There was a meeting this morning.

imperfeito.en: There were a lot of people at the party.
There was no milk.
There used to be a market here.

futuro.en: There's going to be a party on Saturday.
futuro.pt: Vai haver uma festa no sábado.

futuro.en: There's going to be a lot of traffic.
Will there be time?

condicional.en: Would there be a table for two?
There would be no problem.
Without you, there would be no party.

notes.presente: Há never changes for plural: há um café / há três cafés. Há + time = ago (há dois dias) or for (moro aqui há dois anos). Brazilians often say tem for 'there is'; in Portugal use há.
notes.perfeito: Houve = there was / there were for a single event: Houve um acidente.
notes.imperfeito: Havia sets the scene or describes what used to exist: Havia muita gente. Houve is a one-off event; havia is the background.
notes.futuro: In speech use ir + haver: vai haver (there's going to be). Haverá sounds formal, like a news report.

patterns.en: to be going to (determination): Hei de voltar.

compare.ex: Há um café na rua, e eu tenho café em casa.

recap: Há sempre tempo para um café. (There's always time for a coffee.)

intro: Poder means can or may: to be allowed to, or for something to be possible. It's irregular (posso, pude, pôde). When 'can' is about ability or managing after effort, Portuguese usually prefers conseguir.

presente.en: Could you speak more slowly, sir?

perfeito.en: I couldn't go to the party.

perfeito.pt: Não [pudemos] sair por causa da chuva.
perfeito.en: We couldn't go out because of the rain.

perfeito.pt: Eles não [puderam] ficar para o jantar.

imperfeito.pt: Em criança, não [podia] sair à noite.
imperfeito.en: As a child, I wasn't allowed to go out at night.
Could you close the door?
He couldn't eat sugar.
We could go to the cinema.

futuro.en: Tomorrow I'll be able to help you.

futuro.pt: Daqui a um ano [poderás] falar português.
futuro.en: In a year you'll be able to speak Portuguese.
The doctor will be able to see you at three.
You'll be able to go in at nine.

condicional.en: Could I speak to the manager?
Could you give me your number?
He could arrive late.
We could eat out tonight.

imperfeito.en: Could you help me? (formal)
We could go to the beach.
I wasn't allowed to go out.

futuro.en: I'll be able to help you tomorrow.
Will you be able to come?
We won't be able to go.

condicional.en: Could you open the window? (formal)
It could be worse.
Could you repeat that?

notes.presente: Poder = can in the sense of permission or possibility: Posso entrar? Pode chover. Pode ser! = That works / Maybe.
notes.perfeito: Watch the accent: pude (I could) vs pôde (he/she could). The circumflex in pôde separates the past from the present pode.
notes.imperfeito: In Portugal the imperfeito is very common for polite requests and suggestions: Podia ajudar-me? Podíamos ir ao cinema.
notes.futuro: In speech use ir + poder: vou poder, vais poder, não vamos poder.

compare.en: to manage to / to be able to (ability, effort)
compare.ex: Posso entrar? / Não consigo abrir a porta.

compare.en: to know how to (a learned skill)
compare.ex: Sei nadar, mas hoje não posso.

recap: Querer é poder. (Where there's a will, there's a way.)

intro: Conseguir means to manage to, to succeed in or to be able to after some effort. It's an -ir verb with one stem change: eu consigo. Não consigo is the natural way to say 'I can't' when it's about ability.

presente.en: We can already understand almost everything.

perfeito.en: Did you manage to speak to the doctor?
He managed to catch the train.

perfeito.pt: Eles não [conseguiram] bilhetes para o concerto.
perfeito.en: They didn't manage to get tickets for the concert.

imperfeito.en: Before, I couldn't understand anything.

imperfeito.pt: Ela não [conseguia] dormir com o barulho.
imperfeito.en: She couldn't sleep with the noise.

imperfeito.pt: Nós [conseguíamos] ver o mar da janela.
imperfeito.en: We could see the sea from the window.
They always managed to get good seats.

futuro.en: I'll manage to finish by Friday.
You'll manage, I'm sure.
He'll manage to pass the exam.
We'll manage to arrive in time.

condicional.en: I couldn't live without coffee.
Would you be able to do this on your own?
With more time, we would manage to finish.
They would be able to win the game.

perfeito.en: They managed to arrive on time.

imperfeito.en: I couldn't understand the teacher.
She could swim very well.
We couldn't see anything.

futuro.en: You'll manage!
I'm going to manage to finish.
Are we going to manage to arrive on time?

condicional.en: I couldn't do that.
Would you be able to come earlier?
With help, we would manage it.

notes.presente: Only eu changes the stem: consigo. The other forms keep -segu-: consegues, consegue, conseguimos. Não consigo + infinitive = I can't (I'm not able to).
notes.perfeito: Tentei, mas não consegui = I tried, but I didn't manage. Consegui! is how you say 'I did it!'. Conseguimos is the same in the presente and perfeito.
notes.imperfeito: Conseguia = could, over a period of time: Não conseguia dormir (I couldn't sleep, for a while). Consegui = managed, once.
notes.futuro: Vais conseguir! (You'll manage!) is a very common encouragement.

patterns.en: to manage to / to be able to
to manage to arrive in time

compare.ex: Posso fumar aqui? / Não consigo deixar de fumar.
Tentei, mas não consegui.

recap: Tentei muitas vezes e finalmente consegui! (I tried many times and I finally made it!)

intro: Tentar means to try, to attempt or to make an effort to do something. It's a regular -ar verb, and you'll use it constantly when talking about plans, learning something or making an effort.

presente.pt: Eu [tento] falar português todos os dias.
presente.en: I try to speak Portuguese every day.
Do you try to learn new words?

presente.pt: Ela [tenta] fazer exercício três vezes por semana.
presente.en: She tries to exercise three times a week.
We try to understand the problem.
They try to arrive on time.

perfeito.en: Did you try to call me yesterday?
We tried to find a restaurant.
I didn't manage it, but I tried!

imperfeito.en: When I was a child, I used to try to learn piano.
I was trying to speak Portuguese, but it was difficult.
She always tried to help her friends.
We used to try to have dinner together on Sundays.

futuro.en: I'll try again tomorrow.
Will you try to learn Portuguese?
We will try to arrive early.
They will try to win the game.

condicional.en: I would try, but I don't have time.
Would you try again?
He would try to help, if he could.
We would try the new restaurant.

presente.en: Do you understand what I'm trying to say?
presente.pt: Percebes o que estou a tentar dizer?

presente.en: We try to speak Portuguese at home.

perfeito.en: She tried to call me yesterday.
We tried to find the station.

imperfeito.en: When I was younger, I tried to learn piano.
imperfeito.pt: Quando era mais novo, tentava aprender piano.

imperfeito.en: They always tried to arrive early.
You used to try to cook every day.
imperfeito.pt: Tu tentavas cozinhar todos os dias.

futuro.en: We will try again tomorrow.
I'm going to try to find a solution.
Will you try to come?

condicional.en: I would try, but it's too late.
condicional.pt: Eu tentaria, mas é demasiado tarde.

condicional.en: Would you try this dish?
We would try to help.

notes.presente: In Portugal the ongoing present uses estar a + infinitivo: Estou a tentar (I'm trying). Brazil says estou tentando.
notes.perfeito: European spelling: tentámos (Brazil: tentamos). Tentar = to try; conseguir = to manage. Tentei, mas não consegui.
notes.imperfeito: Tentei aprender português = one specific attempt. Tentava aprender português = I was trying / used to try.
notes.futuro: In everyday European Portuguese you'll more often hear ir + infinitivo: vou tentar, vais tentar, vai tentar, vamos tentar, vão tentar.

compare.en: to try something out / to test
compare.ex: Quero experimentar este prato.
Estou a procurar um emprego.

recap: Vou tentar, porque quero conseguir! (I'm going to try, because I want to succeed!)

intro: Dever means should, must or to owe. It expresses advice, duty and probability (Deve ser ali = It must be over there). It's a regular -er verb. For plain necessity Portuguese uses ter de + infinitive: Tenho de trabalhar (I have to work).

quick.en: How much do I owe you?

presente.en: I'm supposed to be home at eight.

perfeito.pt: [Devi] ter deixado o telemóvel no café.
perfeito.en: I must have left my phone in the café.

perfeito.pt: A empresa [deveu] dinheiro aos trabalhadores durante meses.
perfeito.en: The company owed the workers money for months.
They owed their success to their family.

imperfeito.en: I should study more.
You should rest.

imperfeito.pt: Ele [devia] chegar às seis, mas atrasou-se.
imperfeito.en: He was supposed to arrive at six, but he was late.
We ought to go to the doctor.

futuro.en: I should arrive around ten.
The flight is expected to land at five.
We should have the results tomorrow.
Prices are expected to rise.

condicional.en: I should phone my mother.
You ought to apologise.
He should be more careful.
You should visit Porto.

presente.en: How much do I owe you? (formal)

perfeito.en: I had to wait an hour.
I must have lost the key.

imperfeito.en: You should rest.
We should go now.
I had to get up early every day.
imperfeito.pt: Tinha de me levantar cedo todos os dias.

futuro.en: I'm going to have to study more.
The train should arrive at ten.
futuro.pt: O comboio deverá chegar às dez.

futuro.en: You're going to have to wait.

condicional.en: You should see this film.
We should call him.
She shouldn't drink so much coffee.
condicional.pt: Ela não deveria beber tanto café.

notes.presente: Ter de + infinitivo = to have to (necessity): Tenho de trabalhar. Dever + infinitivo = should / must (duty, advice or probability): Deves descansar. Deve estar em casa (He must be at home). In Portugal ter de is preferred to ter que.
notes.perfeito: The perfeito of dever is rare. For 'had to' use ter de: Tive de esperar. Devo ter + participle = I must have...: Devo ter perdido a chave.
notes.imperfeito: Devia / devias / devíamos is the everyday way to say 'should' in Portugal: Devias ir ao médico. Deveria is a bit more formal.
notes.futuro: Deverá often means 'is expected to' (O voo deverá chegar às três). For plans say vou ter de: Vou ter de sair cedo.

compare.ex: Tenho de sair agora, mas devias ficar.
Preciso de descansar.

recap: Tenho de estudar, mas devia descansar. (I have to study, but I should rest.)

intro: Querer means to want, and its imperfeito queria is the polite 'I'd like'. It's irregular: ele quer has no final -e, and the past is quis.

quick.en: I'd like a table for two.
By accident. / I didn't mean to.

presente.en: Do you want to go to the cinema?
She wants to be a doctor.
They want to live in Porto.

perfeito.en: I didn't want to bother you.
Why didn't you want to come?
They insisted on paying for dinner.

imperfeito.en: I'd like a galão (milky coffee), please.
As a child, you wanted to be a footballer.
She wanted to talk to you.
We'd like to book a room.

futuro.en: One day you'll want to come back to Portugal.
Nobody will want to work on Sunday.
After dinner, we'll want to rest.
The kids will want to go to the beach.

condicional.en: I would like to thank everyone.
Would you want to live in another country?
Who would want to go out in this rain?
We would like more information.

presente.en: I want a glass of water.

perfeito.en: I didn't want to bother you.

imperfeito.en: I'd like a coffee, please.
We'd like to book a table.
As a child, I wanted to be a pilot.

futuro.en: You're going to want to come back.
Are you going to want dessert?
They won't want to leave.

condicional.en: Would you want to live in Lisbon?
Who would want that?
We would like to help.

notes.presente: Ele quer has no final -e. Querer takes a noun or an infinitive directly: Quero pão. Quero comer. Querer dizer = to mean.
notes.perfeito: Quis / quiseste / quis are irregular. Não quis often means 'refused': Ele não quis comer.
notes.imperfeito: In cafés and shops, Queria... (I'd like...) is the polite way to ask for something in Portugal. Quereria exists but is rare and formal.
notes.futuro: The synthetic future (quererei) is rare in speech. Say vou querer, vais querer. Vou querer um café is a common way to order.

compare.ex: Gosto muito de café, por isso queria um.

compare.en: to wish / to desire (formal, used by waiters)
compare.ex: Deseja mais alguma coisa?

recap: Queria um café e um pastel de nata, por favor. (I'd like a coffee and a custard tart, please.)

intro: Fazer means to do or to make. It's irregular (faço, fiz, fez, farei) and appears in many everyday expressions: the weather (faz frio), birthdays (fazer anos) and polite requests (faz favor).

presente.pt: Eu [faço] o jantar todos os dias.
O que [fazes] no fim de semana?
presente.en: What do you do at the weekend?
They have their birthday on the same day.

perfeito.en: I made a cake for the party.

perfeito.pt: Ele já [fez] os trabalhos de casa.
perfeito.en: He has already done his homework.
We took a trip to the Azores.

imperfeito.pt: Quando era estudante, [fazia] desporto todos os dias.
imperfeito.en: When I was a student, I did sport every day.
What were you doing in Lisbon?
It was very cold that winter.
We used to have picnics in the park.

futuro.en: I'll do my best.
You'll turn thirty in May.
Tomorrow it will be sunny.
They will have a party on Saturday.

condicional.pt: No teu lugar, eu [faria] o mesmo.
condicional.en: In your place, I would do the same.

condicional.pt: O que [farias] com um milhão de euros?
condicional.en: What would you do with a million euros?
That would make a big difference.
We would do anything for you.

imperfeito.en: It was very cold.
What were you doing there?
We used to do sport.

futuro.en: What are you going to do tomorrow?
I'm going to make soup.
It's going to be sunny.

condicional.en: What would you do?
I would do the same.
That would make sense.

notes.presente: Fazer anos = to have a birthday: Faço anos em junho. Weather: faz frio / faz calor / faz sol. Faz favor (or Se faz favor) = please / excuse me.
notes.perfeito: Irregular stem fiz-: fiz, fizeste, fez, fizemos, fizeram. No accents, and eu fiz vs ele fez.
notes.imperfeito: Use fazia for weather and habits in the past: Fazia sol. Fazíamos isso todos os anos.
notes.futuro: The future and conditional use a short stem far-: farei, faria. In speech prefer ir + infinitivo: vou fazer.

patterns.en: to be needed / to be missed

recap: Faz sol, por isso vou fazer um piquenique! (It's sunny, so I'm going to have a picnic!)

intro: Ir means to go. It's highly irregular, and it's also the main way to talk about the future in Portugal: ir + infinitivo (vou comer = I'm going to eat).

presente.en: Are you going to the party tonight?

presente.pt: Ela [vai] para o trabalho de autocarro.
presente.en: She goes to work by bus.
We're going to eat out today.
They go on holiday in August.

perfeito.en: I went to Sintra on Sunday.
Did you go to the doctor?
Yesterday we went to the beach.

imperfeito.pt: Todos os verões [ia] para casa dos meus avós.
imperfeito.en: Every summer I used to go to my grandparents' house.
Where were you going so early?

imperfeito.pt: Ele [ia] a pé para a escola.
imperfeito.en: He used to walk to school.

imperfeito.pt: Nós [íamos] sair, mas começou a chover.
imperfeito.en: We were going to go out, but it started to rain.

futuro.en: I will go to Lisbon next week.

futuro.pt: Tenho a certeza de que [irás] gostar.
futuro.en: I'm sure you'll like it.
The president will visit the city.
Will you come with us?

condicional.en: I would go with you, but I'm ill.
Would you go and live abroad?
We would go by train.
They said they would go to the party.

perfeito.en: I went to Porto last week.
perfeito.pt: Fui ao Porto na semana passada.

imperfeito.en: I used to go to the beach every day.
imperfeito.pt: Ia à praia todos os dias.

imperfeito.en: I was going to call you.
We used to go on foot.

futuro.en: I'm going to travel in August.
Are you going to come?
It's going to rain.

condicional.en: I would go with you.
Would you go by train?
We would go, but it's late.

notes.presente: Ir + infinitivo is the everyday future in Portugal: vou comer, vais ver, vamos sair. Ir a = a short visit (Vou ao café); ir para = destination or a longer stay (Vou para casa, Vou para Inglaterra).
notes.perfeito: Ir and ser share the same perfeito: fui, foste, foi, fomos, foram. Fui a Lisboa = I went to Lisbon; Fui feliz = I was happy.
notes.imperfeito: Ia + infinitivo = was going to (but didn't): Ia sair, mas fiquei em casa.
notes.futuro: Irei sounds formal. In speech say vou + infinitive. Avoid vou ir: just say vou (Vou amanhã = I'm going tomorrow).

patterns.en: to go by car / train / plane
to walk, to go on foot

compare.ex: Eu vou ao café. Tu vens comigo?

recap: Vamos à praia? Vou já! (Shall we go to the beach? I'm coming right now!)

intro: Vir means to come: movement towards where the speaker is. It's irregular; watch vimos (we come) vs viemos (we came). Vir de = to come from.

presente.en: Are you coming to dinner with us?

presente.pt: O autocarro [vem] daqui a cinco minutos.
presente.en: The bus is coming in five minutes.

presente.pt: Os meus pais [vêm] visitar-me no Natal.
presente.en: My parents are coming to visit me at Christmas.

perfeito.pt: Porque é que não [vieste] à festa?
perfeito.en: Why didn't you come to the party?
We came to pick up the keys.

imperfeito.pt: Antes [vinha] a pé para o trabalho.
imperfeito.en: I used to walk to work.

imperfeito.pt: O meu avô [vinha] sempre ao domingo.
imperfeito.en: My grandfather always came on Sundays.

imperfeito.pt: Nós [vínhamos] de férias para o Algarve.
imperfeito.en: We used to come to the Algarve on holiday.

imperfeito.pt: Eles [vinham] da praia quando os vi.
imperfeito.en: They were coming from the beach when I saw them.

futuro.en: I will come tomorrow morning.
Will you come to my party?
The technician will come on Monday.
The guests will come at eight.

condicional.en: I would come earlier, if I could.
Would you come to Porto with me?
He said he would come later.
Would you come to the dinner?

presente.en: Where does this train come from?

imperfeito.en: I was coming from work.
He used to come every summer.
We used to come here as children.

futuro.en: Are you going to come to the party?
The doctor is going to come tomorrow.
They're coming later.

condicional.en: Would you come with me?
I would come, but I can't.
He said he would come.

notes.presente: Ir vs vir: ir = go (away from the speaker), vir = come (towards the speaker). On the phone, 'I'm coming!' is Vou já!, not venho. Ele vem (he comes) vs eles vêm (they come, with a circumflex).
notes.perfeito: Vim, vieste, veio, viemos, vieram. Don't mix up viemos (we came) with vimos (we come, or we saw from ver).
notes.imperfeito: The imperfeito has -nh- like ter: vinha, vínhamos (compare tinha, tínhamos).
notes.futuro: In speech: vou vir or simply the present: Venho amanhã (I'll come tomorrow).

patterns.en: to come and pick up / fetch
to come on foot / by car

compare.ex: Vou ao café. Vens comigo?
Ele vem de comboio e chega às dez.

recap: Vens jantar cá a casa no sábado? (Are you coming over for dinner on Saturday?)

intro: Ficar is a hugely useful regular -ar verb: to stay, to be located (Onde fica?), to become or end up (ficar contente) and to keep something (fico com este). Only the spelling changes: fiquei.

presente.pt: A farmácia [fica] ao lado do banco.
presente.en: The pharmacy is next to the bank.
We're staying in a hotel near the beach.

perfeito.en: I was very happy with the news.

perfeito.pt: [Ficaste] em casa no fim de semana?
perfeito.en: Did you stay at home at the weekend?
We stayed three days in Évora.

imperfeito.en: When it rained, I used to stay at home.

imperfeito.pt: Tu [ficavas] sempre até tarde no trabalho.
imperfeito.en: You always used to stay late at work.
The school was far from home.

imperfeito.pt: Nós [ficávamos] em casa dos avós no verão.
imperfeito.en: We used to stay at our grandparents' in the summer.

futuro.en: I will stay in Lisbon until Friday.
You'll be surprised.
The restaurant will be closed in August.
They will stay with us for a week.

condicional.pt: Eu [ficaria] mais tempo, mas tenho de ir.
condicional.en: I would stay longer, but I have to go.

condicional.pt: [Ficarias] com o gato este fim de semana?
condicional.en: Would you look after the cat this weekend?
That dress would look good on you.

condicional.pt: Nós [ficaríamos] felizes com a vossa visita.
condicional.en: We would be happy to have you visit.

presente.pt: Onde fica a casa de banho?

perfeito.en: We stayed in a small hotel.

imperfeito.en: We used to stay at my aunt's house.
imperfeito.pt: Ficávamos em casa da minha tia.

imperfeito.en: The house was near the beach.
imperfeito.pt: A casa ficava perto da praia.

imperfeito.en: I always got nervous.

futuro.en: I'm going to stay here.
You're going to be tired.
We're going to stay a week.

condicional.en: I would stay longer.
That would look good.
Would you stay with us?

notes.presente: Use ficar to ask where a place is: Onde fica o museu? (fixed location). For people and things that move, use estar: Onde está o Pedro? Ficar com = to keep / to take: Fico com este.
notes.perfeito: Ficar + adjective = to become / to end up: Fiquei triste (I got sad), Ficou frio (It went cold). Spelling: fiquei (c becomes qu before e). EP accent: ficámos.
notes.imperfeito: Ficava describes where places were and past habits: A escola ficava longe.
notes.futuro: In speech: vou ficar, vamos ficar. Ficar de + infinitive = to agree to / to promise to: Ele ficou de me ligar (He said he'd call me).

compare.ex: Estou em casa. Hoje fico em casa o dia todo.
Ele ficou contente. / Ele tornou-se famoso.

recap: Gosto tanto de Lisboa que vou ficar! (I like Lisbon so much that I'm going to stay!)

intro: Dizer means to say or to tell. It's irregular (digo, disse, direi) and it's the verb for reporting what someone said: Ele disse que vinha.

presente.en: What do you say to this?
How do you say 'thank you' in Portuguese?
They say it's going to rain.

perfeito.en: I said I would be late.

perfeito.pt: Os médicos [disseram] que está tudo bem.
perfeito.en: The doctors said everything is fine.

imperfeito.en: I always used to say yes.

imperfeito.pt: A minha avó [dizia] que tempo é dinheiro.
imperfeito.en: My grandmother used to say that time is money.

imperfeito.pt: Nós [dizíamos] bom dia a toda a gente.
imperfeito.en: We used to say good morning to everyone.
What were they saying?

futuro.en: Tomorrow I'll tell everything.
Will you tell the truth?
Only time will tell.
They'll say they didn't know.

condicional.en: I wouldn't say that.
What would you say to your boss?
Who would have thought!
We would say yes.

presente.en: How do you say 'car' in Portuguese?
They say it's going to rain.

perfeito.en: He told me he was tired.

imperfeito.en: My mother always said that.
imperfeito.pt: A minha mãe dizia sempre isso.

imperfeito.en: What were you saying?
We used to say hello to everyone.
imperfeito.pt: Dizíamos olá a toda a gente.

futuro.en: I'm going to tell him tomorrow.
Time will tell.
What are you going to say?

condicional.en: I wouldn't say that.
Who would have thought!
What would you say?

notes.presente: Dizer = to say / to tell (the content); falar = to speak / to talk (the activity). Diz-me (tell me): in affirmative sentences the pronoun goes after the verb in EP.
notes.perfeito: Disse is both eu and ele/ela. In reported speech the next verb often goes into the imperfeito: Ele disse que estava cansado.
notes.imperfeito: Dizia = used to say. For 'was saying' EP prefers estar a: O que estavas a dizer?
notes.futuro: Short stem dir-: direi, diria. In speech: vou dizer. Quem diria! = Who would have thought!

compare.ex: Ele falou muito, mas não disse nada.
Conta-me o que aconteceu.

recap: Diz-me o que pensas, e eu digo-te o que penso. (Tell me what you think, and I'll tell you what I think.)

intro: Falar means to speak or to talk. It's the model regular -ar verb, so learning it well gives you the pattern for hundreds of others. Falar com = to talk to someone; falar de / sobre = to talk about.

presente.pt: [Falo] inglês e um pouco de português.
presente.en: I speak English and a little Portuguese.

perfeito.en: Yesterday I spoke to my boss.
Have you talked to Maria yet?

imperfeito.en: As a child, I spoke Danish at home.
Who were you talking to on the phone?
We used to talk about the future.
They were all talking at the same time.

futuro.en: I will talk to him tomorrow.

futuro.pt: Daqui a um ano [falarás] português muito bem.
futuro.en: In a year you'll speak Portuguese very well.
The minister will speak on television.
We'll talk about that later.

condicional.pt: Eu [falaria] com ela, mas tenho vergonha.
condicional.en: I would talk to her, but I'm shy.
Would you talk to the teacher for me?
He would speak better if he practised more.
They would never talk like that.

presente.pt: Estou a falar com a minha mãe.

imperfeito.en: We used to speak English at home.
Who were you talking to?
She talked a lot.

futuro.en: I'm going to talk to him.
We're going to talk about that tomorrow.
Are you going to speak Portuguese?

condicional.en: I would speak to the manager.
Would you talk to him?
We would speak more slowly.

notes.presente: Falar com = to talk to: Falo com a minha mãe. Falar de / sobre = to talk about. No article with languages: Falo português. Estou a falar = I'm speaking (Brazil: estou falando).
notes.perfeito: EP spelling: falámos (we spoke) vs falamos (we speak). Brazil writes falamos for both.
notes.imperfeito: Falava = used to speak / was speaking (background). Falei = spoke (one completed event).
notes.futuro: In speech: vou falar, vamos falar. Falamos! (present tense) is a common goodbye: Talk soon!

compare.ex: Ele falou muito, mas não disse nada.

compare.en: to chat / to have a conversation
compare.ex: Gostamos de conversar ao jantar.

recap: Falo pouco português, mas falo todos os dias! (I speak little Portuguese, but I speak it every day!)

intro: Dar means to give. It's irregular in the presente (dou, dás, dá, dão) and the perfeito (dei, deu), and appears in many expressions: dar um passeio, dar jeito, não dá.

quick.en: It's not possible. / It won't work.

presente.en: Will you give me your number?
The window looks out onto the sea.
We go for a walk every Sunday.
The neighbours are throwing a party today.

perfeito.en: I gave my mother a present.
The teacher gave us a lot of homework.
Yesterday we went for a walk along the beach.

imperfeito.en: I used to teach at a school.
My grandfather always used to give me chocolates.
We used to go for long walks in the countryside.
They used to throw parties every Saturday.

futuro.en: I'll give the answer tomorrow.
Will you keep in touch?

futuro.pt: O banco [dará] uma resposta na próxima semana.
futuro.en: The bank will give an answer next week.
You will do your best.

condicional.en: I would give anything for a holiday.
Would you give Ana a lift?
That would be a lot of work.
We would give a hand, if we could.

presente.en: Can you give me the salt?
The room looks onto the garden.
presente.pt: O quarto dá para o jardim.

imperfeito.en: My grandmother always gave me sweets.
imperfeito.pt: A minha avó dava-me sempre doces.

imperfeito.en: I used to teach in Porto.
We used to go for walks.

futuro.en: I'm going to give you a present.
It's going to be a lot of work.
We're going to throw a party.

condicional.en: I would give anything for a coffee.
Would you give Ana a hand?
That would be handy.

notes.presente: Não dá = it's not possible / it doesn't work (very common). Dar jeito = to be handy or convenient. Dar para = to look onto (A janela dá para o mar) or to be enough (Dá para dois).
notes.perfeito: Dar takes -er style endings in the perfeito: dei, deste, deu, demos, deram. Eu dei vs ele deu.
notes.imperfeito: In Portugal the imperfeito is also used for polite wishes: Dava-me jeito uma ajuda (A bit of help would be handy).
notes.futuro: In speech: vou dar, vai dar. Vai dar certo = It's going to work out.

patterns.en: to look onto / to be enough for

compare.en: to give (as a gift) / to offer
compare.ex: Ofereci-lhe flores no aniversário.
Dei-lhe um presente e ele recebeu-o com alegria.

recap: Dá-me um café, se faz favor. (A coffee, please.)

intro: Receber means to receive or to get (a letter, a message, a salary), and also to welcome guests. It's a regular -er verb.

quick.en: I get paid at the end of the month.

presente.en: I get a lot of emails a day.
How much do you earn a month?

presente.pt: Ela [recebe] os clientes com um sorriso.
presente.en: She welcomes customers with a smile.
We have friends over on Saturdays.
The students get their marks tomorrow.

perfeito.en: I received a letter from my grandmother.

imperfeito.pt: Em criança, [recebia] muitos presentes no Natal.
imperfeito.en: As a child, I used to get lots of presents at Christmas.
The hotel used to get a lot of tourists.
We used to get letters every week.
Did you use to get the newspaper at home?

futuro.en: I will get my salary on Friday.
You will get an answer soon.
The winner will receive a thousand euros.
We will welcome the guests at eight.

condicional.pt: Eu [receberia] mais, se trabalhasse ao fim de semana.
condicional.en: I would earn more if I worked at weekends.

condicional.pt: [Receberias] os meus pais em tua casa?
condicional.en: Would you have my parents at your house?
He would never accept money for that.

condicional.pt: Eles disseram que [receberiam] a encomenda hoje.
condicional.en: They said they would get the parcel today.

presente.en: I get a lot of messages.

perfeito.en: I haven't received the parcel yet.

imperfeito.en: We used to have a lot of visitors.
He earned very little.
I used to get letters from my grandmother.

futuro.en: You're going to get a message.
We're going to welcome the guests.
When am I going to get the money?

condicional.en: I would receive more money.
Would they get the letter in time?
condicional.pt: Eles receberiam a carta a tempo?

condicional.en: We would gladly have your friends over.
condicional.pt: Receberíamos os teus amigos com prazer.

notes.presente: Receber also means to get paid: Recebo ao fim do mês. Receber visitas = to have guests over.
notes.perfeito: Recebemos is both 'we receive' and 'we received'. Time words make it clear: Ontem recebemos uma carta.
notes.imperfeito: Recebia = used to receive / was getting regularly. Recebi = received (once).
notes.futuro: In speech: vou receber. Receberá sounds formal, as in official letters.

compare.ex: Ganho pouco, mas recebo sempre a horas.

recap: Recebi a tua mensagem e fiquei muito contente! (I got your message and I was very happy!)

intro: Ver means to see or to watch (television, a film). It's irregular: vejo, vês, vê, veem in the presente and vi, viu in the perfeito.

presente.en: I can't see anything without glasses.
From here we can see the sea.
They watch a lot of Portuguese films.

perfeito.en: Yesterday I saw a great film.
We saw dolphins in the Sado river.

imperfeito.pt: Em criança, [via] desenhos animados todas as manhãs.
imperfeito.en: As a child, I watched cartoons every morning.
Could you see the sea from your room?
We used to see our grandparents on Sundays.
They used to watch the matches at the café.

futuro.en: I'll see what I can do.
You'll see that I'm right.
Time will tell. (Whoever lives will see.)
We'll see tomorrow.

condicional.en: I would watch that film again.
Would you watch the series with me?
With more light, he would see better.
From here you would see the castle.

presente.en: We watch the news every day.
presente.pt: Vemos as notícias todos os dias.

imperfeito.en: I used to watch a lot of TV.
We were watching the news.
You could see the sea from the house.

futuro.en: We'll see.
I'm going to watch a film.
Are you going to see your parents?

condicional.en: I would see that film.
Would you watch it with me?
From here we would see the sea.

notes.presente: Ver = to see / to watch: ver televisão, ver um filme. Olhar = to look (at): olhar para. Since the 1990 spelling reform, veem has no circumflex (old spelling: vêem).
notes.perfeito: Vi, viste, viu, vimos, viram. Nós vimos = we saw (ver), but also we come (vir): context tells you which.
notes.imperfeito: Via-se = you could see / one could see: Via-se o mar da janela.
notes.futuro: Vamos ver (Let's see / We'll see) is far more common than veremos. Vou ver se... = I'll check whether...: Vou ver se está aberto.

compare.ex: Olhei para o céu, mas não vi nada.

recap: Vi o filme ontem e vou vê-lo outra vez! (I saw the film yesterday and I'm going to watch it again!)

intro: Olhar means to look. It's a regular -ar verb and usually takes para: olhar para alguém (to look at someone). Olha! is also a very common way to get someone's attention.

presente.en: I look out of the window every morning.

presente.pt: Porque é que [olhas] para mim assim?
presente.en: Why are you looking at me like that?

presente.pt: Ele [olha] para o relógio a toda a hora.
presente.en: He keeps looking at his watch.
The tourists look at the castle.

perfeito.pt: [Olhei] para o céu e vi uma estrela.
perfeito.en: I looked at the sky and saw a star.
Did you look carefully at the price?
She looked at me and smiled.

imperfeito.en: I used to look at the sea for hours.
The cat was looking at the birds.
We used to look at the stars.
They were looking at each other.

futuro.en: I'll look at that tomorrow.
Will you look after the children?
We'll look to the future with optimism.
Everyone will look at you.

condicional.pt: Eu [olharia] duas vezes antes de atravessar.
condicional.en: I would look twice before crossing.
Would you look after my cat?

condicional.pt: Ele nunca [olharia] para o telemóvel a conduzir.
condicional.en: He would never look at his phone while driving.

condicional.pt: Eles [olhariam] para nós de forma estranha.
condicional.en: They would look at us strangely.

presente.en: Why are you looking at me?
presente.pt: Porque é que estás a olhar para mim?

perfeito.en: I looked out of the window.

imperfeito.en: She was looking at the sea.
imperfeito.pt: Ela estava a olhar para o mar.

imperfeito.en: We used to look at the stars.
Everyone was looking at us.
imperfeito.pt: Toda a gente olhava para nós.

futuro.en: I'm going to look at the photos.
Who's going to look after the children?
Everyone's going to look at you.

condicional.en: I would look again.
Would you look after my cat?
They would look at us.

notes.presente: Olhar para = to look at. Olhar por = to look after. Olha! (tu) / Olhe! (você) start sentences like 'Look, ...' or 'Hey!'.
notes.perfeito: EP accent: olhámos (we looked) vs olhamos (we look).
notes.imperfeito: Olhava sets the scene: Ela olhava para o mar quando o telefone tocou.
notes.futuro: In speech: vou olhar. To 'have a look at something', Portuguese often just uses ver: Vou ver isso.

patterns.en: to look out of the window

compare.ex: Olhei para o céu, mas não vi nada.
Estou a procurar as chaves.

recap: Olha para o céu: que bonito! (Look at the sky: how beautiful!)

intro: Ouvir means to hear or to listen. It's irregular only in the eu form of the presente: ouço. Everything else follows the -ir pattern: ouves, ouvi, ouvia.

presente.en: I listen to music in the car.
We listen to the radio at breakfast.

presente.pt: Eles nunca [ouvem] os conselhos dos pais.
presente.en: They never listen to their parents' advice.

imperfeito.pt: Em pequeno, [ouvia] fado com a minha avó.
imperfeito.en: As a child, I used to listen to fado with my grandmother.
Could you hear the sea from your room?

imperfeito.pt: Ele não [ouvia] nada com o barulho.
imperfeito.en: He couldn't hear anything with the noise.
We used to hear the birds in the morning.

futuro.en: I will listen carefully.
You'll hear about him one day.
The judge will hear the witnesses tomorrow.
We'll listen to the concert on the radio.

condicional.pt: Eu [ouviria] esta música todos os dias.
condicional.en: I would listen to this song every day.
Would you listen to my opinion?

condicional.pt: Com estas janelas, não [ouviríamos] o trânsito.
condicional.en: With these windows, we wouldn't hear the traffic.
At the front, they would hear better.

presente.en: Do you listen to the radio?

perfeito.en: I heard the news on the radio.

imperfeito.en: We used to listen to fado.
I couldn't hear well.
She was listening to music.

futuro.en: I'm going to listen to the new album.
You're going to hear about it.
We're going to listen to the radio.

condicional.en: I would listen to that.
Would you listen to what I have to say?
condicional.pt: Ouvirias o que tenho a dizer?

condicional.en: We would hear the sea.

notes.presente: Only eu is irregular: ouço (you'll also hear oiço, a common EP variant). Ouvir covers both 'hear' and 'listen'; escutar is 'to listen carefully'.
notes.perfeito: Ouvi dizer que... = I heard that... Ouvimos is the same in the presente and perfeito.
notes.imperfeito: Não ouvia nada = I couldn't hear anything (for a while). Não ouvi = I didn't hear (at one moment).
notes.futuro: Ouvir falar de = to hear about: Nunca ouvi falar disso (I've never heard of that). In speech: vou ouvir.

patterns.en: to listen to music / the radio

compare.ex: Ouvi um barulho e fiquei a escutar.

recap: Ouço fado e ouço Portugal. (I listen to fado and I hear Portugal.)

intro: Saber means to know a fact or a piece of information, and to know how to do something (sei nadar). It's irregular (sei, soube). For knowing people or places, use conhecer.

quick.en: Do you know where it is?

presente.en: I don't know where the keys are.

perfeito.en: I found out about the news yesterday.
He knew straight away that it was true.
We only heard about the accident in the evening.

imperfeito.en: I didn't know you were Portuguese.

imperfeito.pt: [Sabias] que o Porto tem seis pontes?
imperfeito.en: Did you know that Porto has six bridges?
Nobody knew what to do.
They knew everything about the city.

futuro.en: Tomorrow I will know the results.
One day you'll know the truth.
Nobody will know about this.
We'll know more next week.

condicional.en: I wouldn't know what to say.
Would you be able to explain this to me?
He would know what to do.
Would you know how to get there on your own?

presente.en: Do you know where the station is?

imperfeito.en: I didn't know!
Did you know that?
She knew the answer.

futuro.en: You're going to know soon.
We're going to know tomorrow.
How am I going to know?

condicional.en: I wouldn't know what to do.
Would you know how to get there?
He would know.

notes.presente: Saber vs conhecer: saber = to know a fact or how to do something (Sei onde ele mora. Sei cozinhar). Conhecer = to be familiar with a person, place or thing (Conheço o Pedro. Conheço Lisboa). Saber bem = to taste good: Este café sabe bem.
notes.perfeito: In the perfeito, saber often means 'to find out': Soube ontem (I found out yesterday). Eu soube and ele soube are the same.
notes.imperfeito: Não sabia! (I didn't know!) is the everyday reaction to news. Sabias que...? = Did you know that...?
notes.futuro: In speech: vou saber, vamos saber.

patterns.en: to know how to / can (a skill)
to know about / to hear about
to taste good / to feel good

compare.en: to know (a person, a place), to be familiar with
compare.ex: Sei onde ele mora, mas não o conheço bem.
Sei nadar, mas hoje não posso.

recap: Não sei nadar, mas sei que vou aprender! (I can't swim, but I know I'm going to learn!)

intro: Conhecer means to know a person, a place or a thing (to be familiar with it), and in the perfeito, to meet someone for the first time. It's a regular -er verb; only the spelling changes in conheço.

quick.en: Nice to meet you. (to a man, formal)

presente.en: I know a good restaurant near here.

presente.pt: Ele [conhece] toda a gente na aldeia.
presente.en: He knows everyone in the village.
We don't know the north yet.

perfeito.en: I met my husband in Coimbra.
We met a lot of nice people on the trip.

imperfeito.en: I didn't know anyone in Lisbon.
Did you already know this place?

imperfeito.pt: O meu avô [conhecia] todas as ruas do Porto.
imperfeito.en: My grandfather knew every street in Porto.
We knew the owner of the café.

futuro.en: I will meet your parents on Sunday.
You'll meet lots of new people.
He will meet the team tomorrow.
You'll get to know the city on foot.

condicional.pt: Eu [conheceria] melhor o país se viajasse mais.
condicional.en: I would know the country better if I travelled more.
Would you know a good dentist?

condicional.pt: Sem aquela festa, ele nunca [conheceria] a Ana.
condicional.en: Without that party, he would never have met Ana.
That way we would get to know the region.

perfeito.en: I met her at a party.

imperfeito.en: I didn't know anyone.
Did you already know him?
She knew the city well.

futuro.en: You're going to meet my parents.
I'm going to get to know Porto.
We're going to meet new people.

condicional.en: I would like to meet her.
Would you know a good doctor?
We would get to know the country.

notes.presente: Saber vs conhecer: conhecer = to know a person, place or thing (Conheço o Pedro. Conheço Lisboa). Saber = to know a fact or how to do something (Sei onde ele mora). Spelling: conheço with ç keeps the soft c sound.
notes.perfeito: In the perfeito, conhecer usually means to meet for the first time: Conheci a Ana em 2019. Conhecemos = we know / we met.
notes.imperfeito: Conhecia = already knew (a person or place): Já conhecia o Porto.
notes.futuro: Vou conhecer can mean 'I'm going to meet' (a person) or 'I'm going to visit / get to know' (a place).

patterns.en: to know / to visit a place

compare.ex: Conheço a Ana, mas não sei onde ela mora.
Conheci a Ana numa festa e hoje encontrei-a no café.

recap: Conheci a Ana em Lisboa e agora conheço a cidade toda! (I met Ana in Lisbon and now I know the whole city!)

intro: Passar means to pass, to go by, to spend (time) and to hand something over. It's a regular -ar verb with many everyday uses: passar férias, passar por, passar no exame.

presente.en: I go past the bakery every morning.
How do you spend your weekends?
We spend the summer in the Algarve.

presente.pt: Os autocarros [passam] de dez em dez minutos.
presente.en: The buses come every ten minutes.

perfeito.en: Did you have a good night?
He spent a week in Madrid.
We spent Christmas with the family.

imperfeito.en: I used to spend hours reading.
You always used to come by here.

imperfeito.pt: O comboio [passava] perto da nossa casa.
imperfeito.en: The train used to go past our house.
We used to spend the holidays in the village.

futuro.pt: [Passarei] por tua casa logo à noite.
futuro.en: I'll drop by your place tonight.
You'll pass the exam, I'm sure.
The pain will go away in a few days.

futuro.pt: Eles [passarão] o Ano Novo no Funchal.
futuro.en: They will spend New Year in Funchal.

condicional.en: I would spend my life travelling.
Would you spend the weekend with us?

condicional.pt: Disseram que o autocarro [passaria] às oito.
condicional.en: They said the bus would come at eight.
We would spend more time together.

presente.en: Can you pass me the bread?

perfeito.en: We spent the weekend in Porto.
perfeito.pt: Passámos o fim de semana no Porto.

imperfeito.en: I used to spend the summers at my grandparents'.
imperfeito.pt: Passava os verões em casa dos meus avós.

imperfeito.en: The bus used to go by here.
We used to spend hours talking.

futuro.en: I'm going to drop by later.
futuro.pt: Vou passar por aí mais tarde.

futuro.en: It's going to pass.
We're going to spend Christmas here.

condicional.en: I would spend more time at home.
Would you drop by tomorrow?
We would spend a week in the Azores.

notes.presente: Passar = to spend time; gastar = to spend money or resources: Passámos o fim de semana no Porto e gastámos muito. O que se passa? = What's going on?
notes.perfeito: Passar no exame = to pass the exam. EP accent: passámos (we spent) vs passamos (we spend).
notes.imperfeito: Passava horas a + infinitive = I used to spend hours doing something: Passava horas a ler.
notes.futuro: Vai passar! = It'll pass! (to comfort someone). Passar por = to drop by / to go through: Vou passar por tua casa.

patterns.pt: passar férias / o fim de semana

patterns.en: to go past / to drop by / to go through

compare.ex: Passei uma semana em Paris e gastei muito dinheiro.

recap: O tempo passa depressa quando passamos férias em Portugal! (Time flies when we spend our holidays in Portugal!)

intro: Gastar means to spend money or to use up resources such as time, energy, water or petrol. It's a regular -ar verb. For spending time on something (holidays, a weekend), use passar.

quick.en: It uses a lot of petrol.

presente.en: I spend a lot of money on books.
How much do you spend a month on food?
We spend too much on restaurants.

perfeito.en: I spent fifty euros at the supermarket.
Did you spend a lot on holiday?

perfeito.pt: Ele [gastou] o salário todo em roupa.
perfeito.en: He spent his whole salary on clothes.
We wasted a huge amount of time in traffic.

imperfeito.en: I used to spend a lot on taxis.
The old fridge used a lot of electricity.
We spent little when we were students.

imperfeito.pt: Eles [gastavam] o dinheiro todo ao fim de semana.
imperfeito.en: They used to spend all their money at the weekend.

futuro.en: This month I will spend less.
With this phone you'll use less battery.
The new heating will use less energy.
We'll spend as little as possible.

condicional.en: I would never spend so much on a dinner.
How much would you spend on a house?
That way, he would use less water.
You would spend less by train.

presente.en: I spend a lot on coffee.
How much do you spend a month?
This car uses a lot of petrol.

imperfeito.en: We used to spend little.
She spent a lot on clothes.
The old car used a lot of petrol.
imperfeito.pt: O carro velho gastava muita gasolina.

futuro.en: I'm going to spend less.
Are you going to spend all that?
We're not going to spend much.

condicional.en: I wouldn't spend that much.
How much would you spend?
We would use less water.

notes.presente: Gastar = to spend money / to use up; passar = to spend time (Passei o dia na praia). Gastar tempo means using up or wasting time: Gastei uma hora no trânsito.
notes.perfeito: EP accent: gastámos (we spent) vs gastamos (we spend).
notes.imperfeito: Gastava = used to spend (a habit): Gastava muito em táxis.
notes.futuro: In speech: vou gastar. The opposite is poupar (to save): Vou poupar para as férias.

compare.ex: Passei o fim de semana em Sintra e gastei pouco.
Este mês vou poupar em vez de gastar.

recap: Gastei pouco, mas passei um dia ótimo! (I spent very little, but I had a great day!)

en: to arrive / to reach / to suffice
intro: Chegar means to arrive, to reach, and also to be enough (Chega! = That's enough!). It's a regular -ar verb; only the spelling changes in cheguei.

presente.en: What time do you arrive tomorrow?

presente.pt: O comboio [chega] às dez e meia.
presente.en: The train arrives at half past ten.

presente.pt: Os meus amigos [chegam] hoje de Londres.
presente.en: My friends arrive from London today.

perfeito.en: I arrived in Lisbon last night.

imperfeito.en: I always used to arrive late for class.
You used to get home very late.
The money wasn't enough for everything.

imperfeito.pt: Quando [chegávamos] à praia, já estava cheia.
imperfeito.en: When we got to the beach, it was already full.

futuro.en: I will arrive around nine.
You'll go far.
The flight will arrive late.
Will you arrive in time?

condicional.pt: Eu [chegaria] mais cedo, mas há muito trânsito.
condicional.en: I would arrive earlier, but there's a lot of traffic.
Would you arrive on time by car?
The money would be enough for the holidays.
Without the GPS, we would never get there.

imperfeito.en: He always arrived late.
The money wasn't enough.
When I used to get home, the children were already asleep.
imperfeito.pt: Quando chegava a casa, as crianças já dormiam.

futuro.en: I'm going to arrive late.
What time are you going to arrive?
The train is going to arrive soon.
futuro.pt: O comboio vai chegar daqui a pouco.

condicional.en: I would arrive on time.
Would it be enough?
We would arrive earlier by train.

notes.presente: Chegar a = to arrive at / in: Chego a Lisboa amanhã (not em). Chegar a casa = to get home. Chega! / Já chega! = That's enough!
notes.perfeito: Spelling: cheguei (g becomes gu before e). EP accent: chegámos (we arrived) vs chegamos (we arrive).
notes.imperfeito: Não chegava = it wasn't enough: O tempo não chegava.
notes.futuro: In speech: vou chegar. Chegar a + infinitive = to get to / to actually do: Chegaste a ver o filme? (Did you get to see the film?)

patterns.en: to get to do / to actually do

compare.ex: O comboio parte às oito e chega às dez.
Ele vem de comboio e chega às dez.

recap: Cheguei a Lisboa e já não quero partir! (I've arrived in Lisbon and I don't want to leave anymore!)

en: to leave / to depart / to break
intro: Partir has two main meanings: to leave or depart (O comboio parte às oito) and, in Portugal, to break (parti um copo). It's a regular -ir verb.

quick.pt: A que horas parte o comboio?
quick.en: What time does the train leave?

presente.en: I leave for Brazil on Monday.
When do you leave on holiday?

presente.pt: O autocarro [parte] da estação às oito.
presente.en: The bus leaves from the station at eight.
We cut the cake into eight slices.

perfeito.en: I broke a glass in the kitchen.
Did you break your leg skiing?

perfeito.pt: O avião [partiu] com uma hora de atraso.
perfeito.en: The plane left an hour late.

perfeito.pt: Os miúdos [partiram] a janela com a bola.
perfeito.en: The kids broke the window with the ball.

imperfeito.en: As a child, I used to break everything.
The last train used to leave at midnight.
We always used to leave at dawn.

imperfeito.pt: Eles [partiam] de Lisboa todos os anos em agosto.
imperfeito.en: They used to leave Lisbon every year in August.

futuro.en: I will leave early tomorrow.
Will you leave on your own?
The ship will depart at six.
We will leave after lunch.

condicional.en: I would never leave without saying goodbye.
Would you leave for another country for love?

condicional.pt: Com este vento, o barco não [partiria].
condicional.en: With this wind, the boat wouldn't leave.
We would leave today, if we could.

imperfeito.en: He was always breaking things.
The boat used to leave at seven.
We used to leave early.

futuro.en: We're going to leave at noon.
Careful, you're going to break that!
When are you going to leave?

condicional.en: Would you leave today?
We would leave earlier.
They would break everything.

notes.presente: In Portugal partir is the everyday verb for 'to break': partir um copo, partir a perna (Brazil: quebrar). Partir-se = to break (by itself): O copo partiu-se.
notes.perfeito: Partimos is both 'we leave' and 'we left'. With body parts no possessive is needed: Parti o braço (I broke my arm).
notes.imperfeito: Partia = used to leave / used to break: O comboio partia às oito.
notes.futuro: For leaving, everyday speech often uses sair (to go out) or ir-se embora (to go away): Vou-me embora. Partir sounds a bit more formal for departures.

patterns.en: to break a glass / one's leg

compare.en: to go out / to leave (a place)
compare.ex: Saio de casa às oito; o comboio parte às nove.
Deixei as chaves em casa.

recap: Parti o telemóvel no dia em que parti para Lisboa! (I broke my phone the day I left for Lisbon!)

intro: Deixar means to leave (something or someone somewhere), to let or allow, and with de + infinitive, to stop doing something (deixar de fumar). It's a regular -ar verb.

quick.en: I left the keys at home.

presente.pt: [Deixo] as crianças na escola às oito.
presente.en: I drop the children at school at eight.

presente.pt: O meu chefe não me [deixa] sair cedo.
presente.en: My boss doesn't let me leave early.

presente.pt: Os pais [deixam] os filhos brincar na rua.
presente.en: The parents let their children play in the street.

perfeito.en: I left my umbrella on the bus.
Where did you leave the car?

perfeito.pt: Ele [deixou] de fumar no ano passado.

perfeito.en: We left a message at reception.

imperfeito.pt: Antes [deixava] sempre tudo para o último dia.
imperfeito.en: I always used to leave everything to the last day.

imperfeito.pt: A minha mãe não me [deixava] ver televisão à noite.
imperfeito.en: My mother didn't let me watch TV at night.
We used to leave the door open in summer.

imperfeito.pt: Eles [deixavam] o cão em casa dos vizinhos.
imperfeito.en: They used to leave the dog at the neighbours'.

futuro.en: I'll leave the key under the mat.
You'll be missed.

futuro.pt: O comboio [deixará] de parar nesta estação.
futuro.en: The train will stop calling at this station.
We will never stop fighting.

condicional.pt: Eu nunca [deixaria] o meu cão sozinho.
condicional.en: I would never leave my dog alone.

condicional.pt: [Deixarias] o teu emprego por uma viagem?
condicional.en: Would you leave your job for a trip?

condicional.pt: Ele [deixaria] de beber café, se pudesse.
condicional.en: He would stop drinking coffee, if he could.

condicional.pt: Eles não te [deixariam] entrar sem bilhete.
condicional.en: They wouldn't let you in without a ticket.

presente.en: I drop the kids at school.

perfeito.en: I left my phone at home.
Where did you leave the car?

imperfeito.en: My parents didn't let me go out.
imperfeito.pt: Os meus pais não me deixavam sair.

imperfeito.en: We used to leave the windows open.
He always left everything on the table.
imperfeito.pt: Ele deixava sempre tudo em cima da mesa.

futuro.en: I'm going to stop eating sugar.
Are you going to let me go?
We're going to leave the car here.

condicional.en: I wouldn't leave you alone.
Would you leave your job?
They wouldn't let us in.

notes.presente: Three key uses: leave something somewhere (Deixo o carro aqui), let / allow (Deixa-me ver), and deixar de + infinitive = to stop doing (Deixei de fumar). Deixa estar = Never mind / Leave it.
notes.perfeito: Deixar = to leave something behind; sair = to leave a place; partir = to depart. Deixei as chaves em casa vs Saí de casa. EP accent: deixámos.
notes.imperfeito: Não me deixavam = they didn't let me (as a rule): Os meus pais não me deixavam sair.
notes.futuro: In speech: vou deixar. Não deixes de + infinitive = make sure you...: Não deixes de visitar Sintra!

compare.en: to go out / to leave (a place)
compare.ex: Saí de casa e deixei a porta aberta.
O comboio parte às dez.

recap: Deixa-me ver... deixei as chaves no carro! (Let me see... I left the keys in the car!)

intro: Procurar means to look for or to search for. It's a regular -ar verb and takes a direct object with no preposition: procuro as chaves (I'm looking for the keys).

presente.en: I'm looking for a room in Lisbon.
She's been looking for work for three months.
We're looking for a cheap restaurant.
They always look for the best solution.

perfeito.pt: [Procurei] o telemóvel em todo o lado.
perfeito.en: I looked for my phone everywhere.
Have you looked on the internet?

perfeito.pt: Ele [procurou] o médico por causa das dores.
perfeito.en: He went to the doctor because of the pain.
We looked for a hotel near the centre.

imperfeito.en: I was looking for a pharmacy when I saw you.
Was this what you were looking for?

imperfeito.pt: O cão [procurava] o dono por todo o lado.
imperfeito.en: The dog was looking everywhere for its owner.
We were looking for a home at that time.

futuro.en: Tomorrow I'll look for another solution.
Will you look for a job in Portugal?
The police will look for the thief.
They will look for a bigger flat.

condicional.en: I would look in another shop.
Would you look for a home in the centre or outside?
He would look for help, if he needed it.
We would look for a quieter place.

perfeito.en: Did you look in the car?

imperfeito.en: I was looking for you.
She was looking for a job.
What were you looking for?

futuro.en: I'm going to look for a new job.
We're going to look for a restaurant.
Are you going to look for a flat?

condicional.en: I would look on the internet.
Where would you look?
We would look for a cheaper hotel.

notes.presente: No preposition: procurar algo = to look for something. Estar à procura de = to be looking for: Estou à procura de casa. Procurar por is used mainly for people: Alguém procurou por mim?
notes.perfeito: Procurar = to look for; encontrar = to find. Procurei as chaves, mas não as encontrei. EP accent: procurámos.
notes.imperfeito: Procurava = was looking for (background): Procurava um táxi quando começou a chover.
notes.futuro: In speech: vou procurar, vamos procurar.

patterns.en: to look for a job / a home
to try to (formal): Procuro fazer o meu melhor.

compare.ex: Procurei, procurei, e finalmente encontrei!
Olha para isto!

recap: Procuro casa em Lisboa: deseja-me sorte! (I'm looking for a flat in Lisbon: wish me luck!)

intro: Encontrar means to find, and also to meet or run into someone. It's a regular -ar verb. Encontrar-se com = to meet up with someone (on purpose).

presente.en: I never find a parking space.
You find everything at the supermarket on the corner.
We find good prices at the market.

perfeito.en: I found five euros in the street.

perfeito.pt: Ontem ele [encontrou] um antigo colega no metro.
perfeito.en: Yesterday he ran into an old colleague on the metro.

imperfeito.pt: Antes [encontrava] sempre os vizinhos no café.
imperfeito.en: I always used to meet the neighbours at the café.
He could never find his keys.
We used to find shells on the beach.
They used to meet every Saturday.

futuro.en: I'll find a solution.

futuro.pt: [Encontrarás] o hotel ao lado da estação.
futuro.en: You'll find the hotel next to the station.
Whoever looks will find.
We'll find time for everything.

condicional.pt: Eu nunca [encontraria] esta rua sem o mapa.
condicional.en: I would never find this street without the map.
Where would you find a good café around here?
He would easily find work in Porto.
We would find the way on our own.

presente.en: Shall we meet at the café?

perfeito.en: I ran into Maria in the street.

imperfeito.en: We used to meet at the café.
He never found anything.
I used to find shells on the beach.

futuro.en: You're going to find it.
We're going to meet at eight.
I'm going to find a solution.

condicional.en: I would never find it.
Where would you find a taxi?
We would find the way.

notes.presente: Encontrar = to find, or to run into someone by chance: Encontrei o Rui no mercado. Encontrar-se com = to meet up (planned): Encontro-me com a Ana às cinco. With nos the final -s drops: encontramo-nos.
notes.perfeito: EP accent: encontrámos (we found) vs encontramos (we find). Procurar = to look for; encontrar = to find.
notes.imperfeito: Encontrava = used to find / used to meet: Encontrava sempre os amigos no café.
notes.futuro: In speech: vou encontrar, vamos encontrar-nos.

patterns.en: to find something / to run into someone

compare.ex: Procurei as chaves e encontrei-as no carro.
Conheci a Ana numa festa; hoje encontrei-a no café.

recap: Quem procura sempre encontra! (Whoever looks will always find!)
